verifiedAgainst: 2026-10-02. Packages: @wordpress/dependency-extraction-webpack-plugin 6.56.0, lib/util.js — `BUNDLED_PACKAGES` (returned `undefined` from `defaultRequestToExternal`, so webpack compiles them into the bundle) and `defaultRequestToHandle` (`@wordpress/<x>` -> `wp-<x>` for every other @wordpress package); WordPress/wordpress-develop trunk (7.2-alpha) src/wp-includes/assets/script-loader-packages.php registers `components.js` and no `ui.js`, so there is a `wp-components` script handle and no `wp-ui` one. Tokens: WordPress/wordpress-develop src/wp-includes/script-loader.php — `wp-theme` is registered as a style (src /wp-includes/css/dist/theme/design-tokens.css) and `wp-components` lists it as a dependency in 7.1.0 and trunk, and in neither 6.9.0 nor 7.0.0; WordPress/gutenberg trunk lib/client-assets.php registers `wp-theme` (build/styles/theme/design-tokens.css) and appends it to `wp-components`' deps, and puts it first in `wp-edit-blocks`. `wp-block-editor` and `wp-commands` depend on `wp-components` in core's `$package_styles`. @wordpress/theme 2.2.0 README: 'WordPress registers the design tokens stylesheet as the `wp-theme` style handle'; a separate app shell or iframe must enqueue it itself; its build plugins (`*-ds-token-fallbacks`, applied automatically by @wordpress/build 0.24.0 when @wordpress/theme is installed — not by @wordpress/scripts 35.0.0) write the generated value into every bare var(--wpds-*) as a fallback.
note: How the WordPress Design System reaches a page, as declared context rather than engine logic. `packages`: `external` means WordPress provides the package as a script handle and dependency-extraction maps the import to it, so adopting it costs the bundle nothing; `bundled` means dependency-extraction leaves it in BUNDLED_PACKAGES and webpack compiles it into the plugin's own bundle — the first import is a new runtime dependency, a larger bundle, a `react` entry in the asset manifest, and test config for its ESM build. `tokens`: the --wpds-* custom properties are defined only by the `wp-theme` stylesheet; a page that does not load it resolves every var(--wpds-*) to nothing, and a declaration with an unresolvable var() is invalid at computed-value time — it drops, it does not fall back. Re-verify the BUNDLED_PACKAGES list against the installed plugin before bumping `version` — it moves between releases.

@wordpress/ui.note: In BUNDLED_PACKAGES; WordPress registers no `wp-ui` script handle, so bundling is the only route.

tokens.note: List 'wp-theme' in the dependency array of the wp_enqueue_style that loads this CSS. WordPress core registers it from 7.1, the Gutenberg plugin before that; on an older core without Gutenberg there is no handle, and the sheet has to be bundled. Build-time fallbacks keep the declarations from dropping, but render the default theme's values whatever the site's theme is, so they do not count as delivery.

evidence.note: `wp-theme` itself. A style depending on `wp-components`, `wp-block-editor`, `wp-edit-blocks` or `wp-commands` gets it transitively only on WordPress 7.1+ or with the Gutenberg plugin active, so it is not counted: name the handle the CSS needs.
The sheet bundled into the project's own CSS. The @wordpress/theme README advises enqueueing `wp-theme` instead inside WordPress.

fallbacks.note: Generated fallbacks in every var(): the declaration renders the default theme's value instead of dropping, and never the site's theme. Not delivery; the finding says it was found.
